title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: Supply data frame element symbols numeric column. ggPSE() maps column fill gradient returns standard ggplot2 object.  Elements data appear neutral grey. result plain ggplot2 object, can keep adding layers:
code: battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35) ) ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance", legend_title = "Battery relevance") ggPSE(battery,       value_col    = "importance",       color_low    = "#f7fbff",       color_high   = "#08519c",       legend_title = "Battery relevance") +   labs(title = "Critical elements for Li-ion batteries") +   theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5))

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: Use groups, periods, lanthanides, actinides display portion periodic table.
code: # Transition metals only ggPSE(battery,       value_col   = "importance",       groups      = c(3, 12),       periods     = c(4, 6),       lanthanides = FALSE,       actinides   = FALSE,       legend_title = "Battery relevance") # Full table without lanthanides and actinides ggPSE(battery,       value_col   = "importance",       lanthanides = FALSE,       actinides   = FALSE,       legend_title = "Battery relevance")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: highlight parameter colors groups elements adds legend entry group.
code: ggPSE(highlight = list(   list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),        color   = "#2166ac",        label   = "Battery metals"),   list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),        color   = "#e63946",        label   = "Rare earth magnets") ))

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_bubble() maps numeric column bubble size clean white background.
code: supply_risk <- data.frame(   symbol = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Dy", "Pt", "Rh", "In", "Ga"),   risk   = c(0.62, 0.91, 0.84, 0.88, 0.52, 0.70, 0.78, 0.65) ) ggPSE_bubble(supply_risk, size_col = "risk",              bubble_color = "#d73027", legend_title = "Supply risk score")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_bar() draws proportional bar inside tile growing chosen edge.
code: ggPSE_bar(supply_risk, value_col = "risk",           bar_side     = "bottom",           bar_color    = "#2166ac",           legend_title = "Supply risk score")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_donut() draws small donut pie chart inside tile showing categorical breakdown — example supply mix country phase composition. Requires ggforce package.  Combine gradient fill encode two variables simultaneously:
code: supply <- data.frame(   symbol   = c("Li","Li","Li", "Co","Co", "Nd","Nd", "Pt"),   category = c("CL","AU","AR", "CD","AU", "CN","RU", "ZA"),   share    = c(0.60, 0.30, 0.10, 0.70, 0.30, 0.80, 0.20, 1.00) )  ggPSE() |>   ggPSE_donut(supply, category_col = "category", share_col = "share",               legend_title = "Producer") # Note: combining gradient fill with donut charts requires ggnewscale # to avoid scale conflicts - planned for a future release criticality <- data.frame(   symbol = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Pt"),   value  = c(0.70, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60) ) ggPSE(criticality, value_col = "value", legend_title = "Criticality") |>   ggPSE_donut(supply, category_col = "category", share_col = "share",               legend_title = "Producer")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_profile() extracts single period, group, f-block row combines line plot numeric property. Requires patchwork.
code: data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity", period = 2) ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "atomic_radius_pm", group = 1) ggPSE_profile(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity",               lanthanides = TRUE)

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_badge() overlays country flags (via optional ggflags package) ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 text codes. Multiple countries per element supported — three flags per tile.  Use hierarchy = TRUE scale flags importance order show_legend = TRUE append country legend. Requires patchwork.  Install ggflags flag icons:
code: supply_single <- data.frame(   symbol  = c("Li", "Co", "Nd", "Pt", "Cu", "Ni", "Ga", "In"),   country = c("CL", "CD", "CN", "ZA", "CL", "PH", "CN", "CN"),   value   = c(0.70, 0.91, 0.85, 0.60, 0.50, 0.55, 0.80, 0.75) ) ggPSE(supply_single, value_col = "value",       color_high = "#b2182b", legend_title = "Criticality") |>   ggPSE_badge(supply_single, country_col = "country") supply_multi <- data.frame(   symbol  = c("Li","Li","Li", "Co","Co", "Nd","Nd"),   country = c("CL","AU","AR", "CD","AU", "CN","RU"),   value   = c(0.70, 0.70, 0.70, 0.91, 0.91, 0.85, 0.85) ) ggPSE(supply_multi, value_col = "value", legend_title = "Criticality") |>   ggPSE_badge(supply_multi, country_col = "country",               hierarchy = TRUE, show_legend = TRUE) remotes::install_github("rensa/ggflags")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_theme() applies pre-built visual theme ggPSE plot.
code: ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance") |>   ggPSE_theme("minimal") ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance") |>   ggPSE_theme("publication") ggPSE() |> ggPSE_theme("crazy", seed = 42)

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE_interactive() adds hover tooltips via ggiraph package. Renders HTML documents, Shiny apps, RStudio Viewer.
code: data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE_interactive(   ggpse_elements,   value_col    = "electronegativity",   tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", "block", "electronegativity"),   legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)" )

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: ggPSE ships ggpse_elements, data frame 17 physical chemical properties 118 elements sourced IUPAC 2021 NIST WebBook.
code: data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "electronegativity",       color_low    = "#f7f7f7",       color_high   = "#d73027",       legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)") ggPSE(ggpse_elements, value_col = "melting_point_K",       color_high   = "#08519c",       legend_title = "Melting point (K)")

title: Getting started with ggPSE
text: Use ggPSE_save() sensible periodic table defaults, ggsave() directly full control.
code: p <- ggPSE(battery, value_col = "importance")  # Convenience wrapper with PSE-optimised defaults ggPSE_save(p, "battery.png") ggPSE_save(p, "battery.pdf")  # Full control with ggsave ggsave("battery.png", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm", dpi = 300) ggsave("battery.svg", p, width = 18, height = 8, units = "cm")

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: ggPSE_interactive() wraps standard ggPSE() output ggiraph interactivity. Every tile becomes hoverable, showing configurable tooltip element details. vignette shows use Quarto HTML document.

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
code: # Install ggPSE remotes::install_github("VJGeiger/ggPSE")  # Install ggiraph (required for interactivity) install.packages("ggiraph")

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: simplest call mirrors ggPSE() — pass data frame value column. Hovering tile shows element symbol, atomic number, value.
code: library(ggPSE)  battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35) )  ggPSE_interactive(battery,                   value_col    = "importance",                   legend_title = "Battery relevance")

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Use tooltip_cols control appears hover tooltip. column present data frame can included.
code: data(ggpse_elements)  ggPSE_interactive(   ggpse_elements,   value_col    = "electronegativity",   tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", "block",                    "electronegativity", "ionization_energy_eV"),   legend_title = "Electronegativity (Pauling)" )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: ggPSE_interactive() supports highlight parameter ggPSE(). Hover still works tiles including highlighted ones.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   highlight = list(     list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),          color   = "#2166ac",          label   = "Battery metals"),     list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),          color   = "#e63946",          label   = "Rare earth magnets")   ) )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: groups, periods, lanthanides, actinides parameters work exactly ggPSE(). , transition metals shown.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   ggpse_elements,   value_col   = "melting_point_K",   groups      = c(3, 12),   periods     = c(4, 6),   lanthanides = FALSE,   actinides   = FALSE,   legend_title = "Melting point (K)" )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Control hover fill color tooltip styling via hover_fill hover_stroke.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   battery,   value_col    = "importance",   hover_fill   = "#2166ac",   hover_stroke = "#ffffff",   legend_title = "Battery relevance" )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Adjust width_svg height_svg (inches) fit document layout.
code: ggPSE_interactive(   battery,   value_col  = "importance",   width_svg  = 10,   height_svg = 4 )

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
text: Works format: html . PDF Word output, use ggPSE() instead wrap chunk #| eval: !knitr::is_latex_output(). Shiny, use ggiraph::girafeOutput() ggiraph::renderGirafe() instead calling ggPSE_interactive() directly render function. interactive output embedded GitHub README directly. Use GIF README link hosted HTML version via GitHub Pages.

title: Interactive periodic table in Quarto
code: library(shiny) library(ggPSE) library(ggiraph)  ui <- fluidPage(   titlePanel("Interactive Periodic Table"),   sidebarLayout(     sidebarPanel(       selectInput("prop", "Property",                   choices = c("electronegativity", "melting_point_K",                               "density_g_cm3", "ionization_energy_eV"))     ),     mainPanel(       girafeOutput("pse", width = "100%", height = "500px")     )   ) )  server <- function(input, output) {   output$pse <- renderGirafe({     data(ggpse_elements)     ggPSE_interactive(       ggpse_elements,       value_col    = input$prop,       tooltip_cols = c("name", "atomic_weight", input$prop),       legend_title = input$prop     )   }) }  shinyApp(ui, server)

title: ggPSE — Periodic Table Visualization
text: numeration can switched show_atomic_number = TRUE, default FALSEto avoid crowded tiles. ### Tile borders Adapt tile coloring well borders whole PSE.

code: ggPSE(highlight = list(   list(symbols = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P"),        color   = "#2166ac",        label   = "Battery metals"),   list(symbols = c("Nd", "Dy", "Tb", "Pr", "La", "Ce"),        color   = "#e63946",        label   = "Rare earth magnets") ))

title: ggPSE — Periodic Table Visualization
text: Map numeric variable fill color gradient across elements.  mapping can also applied selection PSE.  also possible customize ggplots multigradient scales better visualization.
code: battery <- data.frame(   symbol     = c("Li", "Co", "Ni", "Mn", "Fe", "P", "C"),   importance = c(0.95, 0.88, 0.75, 0.60, 0.45, 0.40, 0.35) )  ggPSE(battery,       value_col    = "importance",       color_low    = "#f7fbff",       color_high   = "#08306b",       legend_title = "Battery relevance") data(ggpse_elements) ggPSE(ggpse_elements[ggpse_elements$block == "d", ],       value_col = "density_g_cm3", legend_title = "Density (g/cm3)") data(ggpse_elements)  ggPSE(ggpse_elements,       value_col    = "density_g_cm3",       color_low    = "#2166ac",          color_high   = "#a50026",          legend_title = "Density (g/cm³)") +   ggplot2::scale_fill_gradientn(     colours  = c("#2166ac", "#1a9850", "#a50026"),     na.value = "#f0f0f0",     name     = "Density (g/cm³)"   ) +   ggplot2::labs(title = "Elemental density across the periodic table") +   ggplot2::theme(plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

title: ggPSE — Periodic Table Visualization

code: supply <- data.frame(    symbol   = c("Li","Li","Li", "Co","Co", "Nd","Nd", "Pt"),    category = c("CL","AU","AR", "CD","AU", "CN","RU", "ZA"),    share    = c(0.60, 0.30, 0.10, 0.70, 0.30, 0.80, 0.20, 1.00)  )  ggPSE(groups = c(3,12)) |> gPSE_donut(supply, category_col = "category", share_col = "share", plot_all = FALSE)

title: Plot a periodic table with a continuous value overlay — ggPSE
code: ggPSE(   data = NULL,   value_col = NULL,   symbol_col = "symbol",   label_value = TRUE,   value_digits = 2,   color_low = "#fdf0f2",   color_high = "#9a031e",   color_na = "#f0f0f0",   tile_border = NULL,   highlight = NULL,   legend_title = NULL,   show_atomic_number = FALSE,   base_size = 10,   groups = NULL,   periods = NULL,   lanthanides = TRUE,   actinides = TRUE )

title: Plot a periodic table with a continuous value overlay — ggPSE
text: data data frame containing element symbols value column. NULL, blank table using NA color drawn. value_col Character. Column name data map fill color. symbol_col Character. Column data containing element symbols. Default "symbol". label_value Logical. Print numeric values inside tiles. Default TRUE. value_digits Integer. Decimal places displayed values. Default 2. color_low Hex color low end gradient. Default "#fdf0f2". color_high Hex color high end gradient. Default "#9a031e". color_na Hex color elements data. Default "#f0f0f0". tile_border Hex color tile borders. NULL (default), grey border light backgrounds, transparent dark. Set "transparent" suppress. highlight list highlight groups. group list : symbols Character vector element symbols highlight. color Fill color highlighted tiles. label Optional legend label group. Example: list(list(symbols = c("Li","Co"), color = "#2166ac", label = "Battery metals")) legend_title Character. Legend title. Defaults value_col. show_atomic_number Logical. Show atomic numbers top-left tile. Default FALSE. base_size Numeric. Base font size pt. Default 8. groups Integer vector length 2. Range IUPAC groups (columns) display, e.g. c(3, 12) transition metals . Default NULL shows groups. periods Integer vector length 2. Range periods (rows 1-7) display, e.g. c(4, 6) periods 4 6. Default NULL shows periods. Note: lanthanides actinides controlled separately via lanthanides actinides. lanthanides Logical. Show lanthanide row. Default TRUE. actinides Logical. Show actinide row. Default TRUE.

code: ggPSE_badge(   plot = NULL,   data,   symbol_col = "symbol",   country_col = "country",   badge_size = NULL,   hierarchy = FALSE,   hierarchy_scale = c(1, 0.7, 0.5),   show_legend = FALSE,   legend_position = c("right", "left", "bottom", "top"),   legend_size = 0.15,   legend_flag_size = 5,   legend_text_size = 9,   base_size = NULL,   x_anchor = 0.38,   y_anchor = 0.35,   flag_spacing = 0.38,   badge_color = "#333333" )

title: Overlay country-of-origin badges on a periodic table — ggPSE_badge
text: plot ggplot object. NULL blank table created. data data frame element symbols country codes. symbol_col Character. Column containing element symbols. Default "symbol". country_col Character. Column containing ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes. Default "country". badge_size Numeric. Flag text badge size. Default 3.5 flags. hierarchy Logical. Scale flags order - first country largest. Default FALSE. hierarchy_scale Numeric vector length 3. Scale factors 1st, 2nd, 3rd flag. Default c(1.0, 0.70, 0.50). show_legend Logical. Append country legend. Requires patchwork. Default FALSE. legend_position Character. "right" (default), "left", "bottom", "top". legend_size Numeric. Relative size legend vs main plot. Default 0.15. legend_flag_size Numeric. Flag size legend. Default 5. legend_text_size Numeric. Text size legend. Default 9. base_size Numeric. Base font size. Default NULL. x_anchor Numeric. Horizontal position rightmost flag. Default 0.38. y_anchor Numeric. Vertical position flags. Default 0.35. flag_spacing Numeric. Spacing flags. Default 0.38. badge_color Character. Text color fallback badges. Default "#333333".
